holidays.name: National Love a Tree Day
holidays.description: A day to step outside, appreciate the trees around you, and maybe give one a big, awkward hug. Celebrants are encouraged to plant, admire, or simply say thank you to their leafy neighbors.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance that appears on many American holiday calendars, promoted by tree-loving groups and holiday-listing sites. It has no single credited founder.
holidays.funFact: A single mature tree can absorb roughly 48 pounds of carbon dioxide per year and release enough oxygen for a couple of people to breathe.

holidays.name: National Barbecue Day
holidays.description: A smoky salute to grilling, slow-cooking, and sauce-slathering. Backyard pitmasters fire up the grills and argue passionately about whose sauce and technique are best.
holidays.origin: An informal food observance celebrated in the United States as grilling season kicks off in late spring. It is promoted mainly by food brands and holiday calendars rather than by any official proclamation.
holidays.funFact: The word 'barbecue' is widely believed to come from 'barbacoa,' a word the Spanish borrowed from the Taíno people of the Caribbean for a wooden framework used to cook meat.

holidays.name: National Coconut Cream Pie Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to the creamy, toasty, tropical dessert with flaky crust, custard filling, and mountains of whipped cream and toasted coconut. Pie lovers everywhere are given a perfect excuse for dessert.
holidays.origin: A food-industry-style unofficial holiday listed on American food calendars. Its exact founder is unknown, but it fits the tradition of dedicating days to classic diner desserts.
holidays.funFact: Coconuts are technically not nuts but drupes, the same fruit category as peaches and cherries.

holidays.name: International Day of Light
holidays.description: A UN-recognized celebration of light and its role in science, culture, art, education, and sustainable development. It encourages people to appreciate everything from sunrise to lasers.
holidays.origin: Proclaimed by UNESCO in 2017 to mark the anniversary of the first successful operation of the laser, demonstrated by physicist Theodore Maiman on May 16, 1960.
holidays.funFact: Maiman's first laser used a synthetic ruby crystal, and it was reportedly rejected by a leading journal before the discovery became world famous.

holidays.name: Biographers Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate those who spend years digging through letters, archives, and gossip to tell the stories of other people's lives. It is a chance to read a biography and thank its patient author.
holidays.origin: Observed on May 16 in honor of the date in 1763 when James Boswell first met Samuel Johnson, a meeting that led to Boswell's celebrated biography, The Life of Samuel Johnson.
holidays.funFact: Boswell's book is often called one of the greatest biographies in the English language, and it was famously based on his obsessive note-taking about Johnson's conversations.
